title: Columbus reaches the mainland
description: On his third voyage Columbus lands on the Paria Peninsula, the first recorded European landing on the South American mainland.

title: Coro founded
description: Juan de Ampíes founds Coro, the first capital of the Province of Venezuela.

title: Welser concession
description: Charles V grants the Welser bankers of Augsburg the right to colonise Venezuela, which they hold until 1546.

title: Caracas founded
description: Diego de Losada founds Santiago de León de Caracas, the later capital.

title: Guipuzcoan Company founded
description: A Basque trading company receives a monopoly on Venezuela's trade with Spain, chiefly in cacao.

title: Captaincy General of Venezuela
description: Charles III joins the provinces of Venezuela under one government in Caracas, outlining the later country.

title: Miranda lands at Coro
description: Francisco de Miranda lands with a small force and raises the tricolour flag, but finds no support and withdraws.

title: Caracas junta
description: The city council of Caracas deposes the Spanish captain general and sets up a governing junta.

title: Declaration of independence
description: A congress of seven provinces declares Venezuela independent of Spain, the first such declaration in Spanish America.

title: Caracas earthquake
description: An earthquake destroys Caracas and other republican towns, hastening the fall of the First Republic.

title: Admirable Campaign
description: Bolívar enters Caracas after marching from New Granada and founds the Second Republic.

title: Battle of Carabobo
description: Bolívar defeats the main royalist army, deciding the independence of Venezuela.

title: Battle of Lake Maracaibo
description: The republican fleet under José Prudencio Padilla defeats the Spanish squadron, ending Spanish resistance in Venezuela.

title: Separation from Gran Colombia
description: A congress at Valencia makes Venezuela a separate republic with José Antonio Páez as president.

title: Slavery abolished
description: President José Gregorio Monagas signs the law freeing the remaining slaves.

title: Federal War
description: Liberals rising at Coro begin a war against the conservative government that is the deadliest in the republic's history and ends in a federal victory.

title: Guzmán Blanco takes Caracas
description: Antonio Guzmán Blanco takes the capital and begins nearly two decades of dominance over Venezuelan politics.

title: Naval blockade of Venezuela
description: Britain, Germany and Italy blockade Venezuelan ports to force payment of debts, leading the United States to extend the Monroe Doctrine.

title: Gómez seizes power
description: Juan Vicente Gómez takes power while President Castro is abroad and rules as dictator until 1935.

title: Barroso II blowout
description: An oil well blows out near Lake Maracaibo, showing the size of the reserves that make Venezuela a leading oil exporter.

title: Coup of October 1945
description: Young officers and the Democratic Action party overthrow President Medina, opening three years of elected government.

title: Fall of Pérez Jiménez
description: A rising of civilians and the armed forces drives out the dictator Marcos Pérez Jiménez and begins forty years of elected governments.

title: Oil industry nationalised
description: The state takes over the oil industry and the state company PDVSA begins operating.

title: Caracazo
description: Riots against price rises spread through Caracas and are put down by the army with hundreds of deaths.

title: Chávez's coup attempt
description: Army officers led by Hugo Chávez fail to overthrow President Carlos Andrés Pérez.

title: Chávez elected
description: Hugo Chávez wins the presidency, ending the rule of the two established parties.

title: Vargas tragedy
description: Mudslides after heavy rain kill thousands on the coast of Vargas state, on the day voters approve a new constitution.

title: Coup attempt of 2002
description: Chávez is removed from office after deaths at an opposition march and returns to power two days later.

title: Death of Chávez
description: Hugo Chávez dies after fourteen years in power and is succeeded by Nicolás Maduro.

title: Presidential crisis
description: Juan Guaidó, head of the National Assembly, declares himself acting president in a challenge to Maduro recognised by many countries.
